result.keyword: What's the best project management tool for a startup?
result.markdown:
For most startups, **I'd recommend Linear as the best overall project management tool**, particularly if you're building a tech product or SaaS business.

However, the best choice depends on your team's size, working style, and whether you need product development, general project management, or an all-in-one workspace.

Here's how I'd compare the leading options.

## Best project management tools for startups

![Fast growing startups are built on Linear](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/piHpddRS6n9dTggcCRU3QzspXui7xfTg4qksC0xamyVTz0l5rmZLEYCGsVB7KKUouzfiOTbe-9ydzUq7UB2MFrNbZIGlaUSNjP0C8Bhd2CXnbxL2xZ05zw3USDTcATN8Ed4Fr3ygsGaA-sAB5VFRUeF1jd3BNolTylsoZGFQvpYkliFtHTL_AgaQh3gID9Z3?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. Linear**

(My top pick for tech startups)

- Excellent for product roadmaps, sprint planning, bugs and engineering tasks.
- Fast, clean interface with minimal administrative overhead.
- Great for teams working with GitHub.
- Less suitable for managing every business function.
  
  [Linear website](https://linear.app/)

---

![Finastra Customer Story | ClickUp™](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/OXxUksa73j7hoTxbYQ6zo3pspX36GflPBLMsRWXjhfWZTJdFq6md_tXaxCCc_3Kjh0xQSrUSgXoCYi3d5TOe48r-mvzFwLplQbgf4lhsH3q_bsATt_hAcyva5qI1DtZG8OasgRxxldReZAIfURcJdNdt2Br8nPVvqn-lCO5aR2MxpFl9QAiCxibf4gzehOOb?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. ClickUp**

(Best all-in-one option)

- Tasks, projects, documents, goals and dashboards.
- Highly customisable.
- Good for marketing, operations, sales and product teams.
- Can become overwhelming if overconfigured.
  
  [ClickUp website](https://clickup.com/)

---

![How Notion’s product team brings context and clarity to work (with a template you can use)](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/lB_DgkYrcKsSrK75HhI-s1e0YZmsm9h_ko94aVDn4A57_H0BYO6jOLX7YhGfoLV-bb4yZopgv2ajtj1n2We49qlpkk2pSieb2pIRviX_-Hr7lmml6M-YGw3ewQrsNynTN4ECfMG5mdrQ4ymJ88hPWB0GVS25bKPyi-T-D3MjbFToeY3dypV9fuSvgJ-n9TsY?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Notion**

- Best for early-stage startups.
- Combines company wiki, meeting notes, documentation and task tracking.
- Flexible and easy to customise.
- Not as strong for complex project execution.
  
  [Notion website](https://www.notion.com/)

---

![Introducing Status for remote work • Asana](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/JoierB-tO_00cduG2D81oKuCvdoyZCElp3bd35lcWALcBpW38axGIp0CC5GaQbqWOOkxY6bkkYIgINigcMs7b9WeuaVIp_po7Lw148-t-fKTF_zSNsVOvmWGGRaLv9NtvMW858uJe_Q2tTfzckYfVF8jui4Tyz-v30ONFO8slcrt9_8tb3TIFzeV-apOQxtA?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Asana**

- Excellent for cross-functional teams.
- Clear task ownership and deadlines.
- Strong project timelines and dependencies.
- More structured than many early-stage teams need.
  
  [Asana website](https://asana.com/)

---

![Portfolio management - All Projects Dashboard – Support](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/-5NH-hROEcQXpSQPmMUJv0x7GODAoqXeNRlBaAmeb5yjL6ws1fsUSsHXZKs7cGHwGwKjC6qsKZvaA0-fO7oD8-9_bc-PbX0_EJ1QpOPifoMbrdCVNNuollQzaJIhYGySdgXpxRYlPlDaiOA8sl0RXCUZIj48mjl4S_hb7oB4Rygmeul72nI4kZxZvS769XKO?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. monday.com**

- Great visual dashboards.
- Strong for operations, marketing and business processes.
- Useful automation and reporting.
- Can become expensive as the team grows.
  
  [monday.com website](https://monday.com/)

These choices reflect the main differences in startup workflows, rather than assuming one tool is best for every team. [www.techrepublic.com](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/project-management-software-for-startups/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[waveup.com](https://waveup.com/blog/7-best-project-management-software-for-startups-in2025/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[cloudappcritic.com](https://cloudappcritic.com/project-management/project-management-tools-for-startups/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## My recommendation by startup stage

| Startup situation | My choice |
|--------|--------|
| 1–5 people, pre-launch | Notion |
| 5–15 people, tech startup | Linear |
| 5–20 people, mixed team | ClickUp |
| 20–50 people, scaling | Asana |
| Operations-heavy startup | monday.com |


## What I'd actually set up

For a typical early-stage tech startup, I'd start with just two tools\:

- **Linear\:** All tasks, product development, priorities, bugs and roadmaps.
- **Notion\:** Company documentation, business strategy, meeting notes, processes and knowledge base.

This gives you structure without making project management a full-time job.

What kind of startup are you building?
